15: Kasavana & Smith crosses popularity with contribution margin in dollars. Miller crosses popularity with food cost %. Pavesic crosses food cost % with the margin weighted by units. Goal Value (Hayes & Huffman) adds the weight of labor and other variable costs WITHOUT dropping food cost %: that's why its final factor is (1 − (labor % + other variable % + food cost %)) and not just labor + other. None of them measures all three variables at once: that's why they disagree.
16: The classic popularity threshold is 70% of the average mix: threshold = factor ÷ number of dishes in the category with sales. Raise it if the category is very short.
17: When the four methods agree, it does NOT mean "more certainty": it means the dish is so good or so bad that it shows from any angle. The interesting part is in the rows where they disagree.
18: Contribution margin is the dollar left over to pay for labor, rent and utilities. Food cost % measures efficiency. A dish can be efficient and bring in little money, and the other way round.
